newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit recovers but market remains jittery.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit recovers but market remains jittery.

text.p: The ringgit recovered in early Asian trading on profit-taking of dollar/ringgit positions after heavy selling of the Malaysian unit on Wednesday, dealers said.

"The market looks a bit squarish at the moment, maybe people don't know what to do," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur. "Dollar/ringgit came down quite fast this morning but I expect some buying on dips."
Dealers said demand for the dollar from offshore centres would continue to weigh on the ringgit.
But worries about further intervention by Bank Negara Malaysia was limiting activity, they said.
Dealers said the central bank intervened strongly at 2.5250 late on Wednesday to stem the dollar's rise. A dealer with a European bank in Singapore said as high as $700 million could have been sold.

The Malaysian unit came under heavy selling from foreign funds on Wednesday as weakness in the Thai baht, due to rising concerns about the slowing Thai economy and rumours of political turmoil within that country's cabinet, spilled over to regional currencies including the ringgit.
Dealers said softer dollar/majors also helped the ringgit's recovery.
At 0200 GMT, ringgit was at 2.5155/65 a dollar against 2.5240/50 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday. It had fallen to as low as 2.5260, its lowest level since January 3.
